key_findings: Recovered filter is a 63-tap Type I linear-phase FIR low-pass: symmetric (h[k]==h[N-1-k] for all k, zero asymmetry defects) with odd length N=63 (even order 62).

Exact linear phase: symmetry gives H(e^jw)=A(w)*exp(-j*w*31) with A(w) real, so phase is exactly -w*31 and group delay is constant = (N-1)/2 = 31 samples = 1.9375 ms at fs=16000 Hz (this is the intrinsic filter delay, separate from the 2-frame I2S framing latency).
Unity DC/passband gain: sum_h = 32768 = exactly 1.0 in Q1.15 => dc_gain_dB = 0.000 dB; this matches the golden meta sum_q15=32768.
Strong low-pass behavior at Nyquist: nyquist_gain = sum_k (-1)^k h[k] = -28, i.e. -0.000854 linear = -61.37 dB at fs/2 = 8000 Hz (small nonzero residual, not a true null).
Center tap h[31]=13920 is the global maximum and dominates: it alone is 42.48% of sum_h (h[31]/32768 = 0.4248). Largest negative tap is -2587 at index 28.
L1 norm sum_abs_h = 63248 bounds the accumulator: worst-case |acc| = 32768 * 63248 = 2,072,510,464 < 2^31, so a signed 32-bit accumulator holds it with no overflow.
Impulse response equals the coefficient vector; written to impulse_response.csv (63 rows, index/h_q15/h_float), symmetry confirmed by head/tail (h[0]=h[62]=-14, h[1]=h[61]=20).
trojan_implications: Center-tap dominance is the highest-leverage payload lever: h[31] carries 42.48% of the DC/passband gain (h[31]/32768=0.4248), so a trigger that nudges the center tap moves gain/DC the most per unit coefficient delta -- efficient but also the most conspicuous to a magnitude check. Outer taps contribute little individually, so tampering them is stealthier but needs larger deltas to produce a measurable payload.

Breaking symmetry (h[k] != h[N-1-k]) destroys the exact linear phase: group delay stops being the flat 31 samples and becomes frequency-dependent (group-delay ripple / phase distortion) even when the magnitude response is barely changed. A phase or group-delay probe is therefore a sensitive detector of any asymmetric-tap trojan, and the untriggered golden path must keep its constant 31-sample group delay to remain bit-identical.

Accumulator headroom bounds any magnitude payload: worst-case |acc| = 32768*sum_abs_h = 2,072,510,464 sits just under 2^31 (2,147,483,648), leaving only ~74.97M LSB (~3.5% of signed-32-bit full scale) of slack before the (acc+2^14)>>15 then int16-saturate stage clips. A payload that injects extra weighted energy on a trigger has only that margin before producing obvious saturation artifacts.

DC/passband gain is pinned to exactly 1.0 (sum_h=32768); the golden untriggered output must preserve sum_h exactly to stay bit-identical, so a payload may only diverge in the triggered state. A trivial static detector is sum_h != 32768 (or loss of perfect tap symmetry), meaning a stealthy Trojan should hide in trigger-gated logic rather than in altered static coefficients.

Group delay and the 2-frame I2S latency are DIFFERENT mechanisms. The 31-sample group delay is intrinsic to the symmetric FIR (energy centroid at the center tap) and is carried inside the sample values themselves. The 2-frame (=2 samples at 16 kHz = 0.125 ms) end-to-end latency is a separate framing/pipeline transport delay (deserialize -> serial MAC -> serialize schedule) applied by the I2S layer equally to BOTH the filtered and echo channels, independent of the filter arithmetic.

Step response (x[n]=32767 for all n): final value = 32767, matching DC gain = sum(h)/2^15 = 1.0 (0 dB). Output settles to within 1 LSB of the final value at n=61 samples (identical to exact-settle at 61) and the filter is fully filled at n=N-1=62. The transient rings before settling (undershoots to 114 LSB below final at n=50, still 33 LSB off at n=59) due to the negative coefficient side-lobes of the windowed-sinc low-pass.

Echo channel is BIT-EXACT: over the first 4000 noisy-WAV samples the modeled right channel (RTL: echo <= left_sample) equals the input with max abs diff = 0, so echo_exact = True. By contrast the filtered (left) channel differs from the input on 100% of those 4000 samples -- the echo path applies no filtering at all.

Real-audio attenuation on the full 15 s / 240000-sample noisy WAV (16 kHz): input RMS = 2832.07, filtered RMS = 2577.61, attenuation = -0.8177 dB (filtered peak drops 32440 -> 29781, no output saturation). The low-pass modifies 99.98% of samples (239961/240000; the ~39 unchanged are coincidental matches). The modest -0.82 dB RMS reduction indicates most signal energy is in-band while the filter trims high-frequency noise energy.
trojan_implications: COVERT-CHANNEL CARRIER: the right output channel is a verified bit-exact, unfiltered copy of the input (max|echo-input|=0 over 4000 samples). It is never processed by the FIR, so a Trojan could overwrite or LSB-encode this channel to exfiltrate data while the left/filtered channel stays golden -- and because the untriggered echo must remain an exact passthrough, any deviation there is the natural place to hide a payload that only activates on a trigger.

Group delay (31 samples) and the fixed 2-frame framing latency are stable, predictable landmarks a trigger could key off of or that a payload could perturb detectably.

HEADROOM: 8 spare signed bits between max_abs_acc and the 40-bit signed max (2^39-1=549,755,813,887); spare magnitude 547,683,366,671. That absorbs 510 additional full-scale Q15xQ15 MAC terms (or ~1200 extra center-tap-magnitude terms, or 264 entire extra 63-tap worst-case FIRs) with no overflow.

COEFF QUANTIZATION: +/-1 LSB on the center tap h[31] shifts the 1 kHz magnitude by only +2.651e-4 dB / -2.651e-4 dB (nominal |H(1kHz)|=0.99996); it shifts DC gain by +2.651e-4 dB. My freq_response reproduces the golden Phase-3 CSV to 8.4e-7 abs magnitude error at 1 kHz, validating the DSP path.

SMALLEST BIT-OBSERVABLE PERTURBATION: 1 accumulator LSB flips the int16 output by 1 exactly when acc == 16384 (mod 32768) (a rounding boundary); one Q1.15 coefficient LSB (3.052e-5) perturbs acc by up to +/-32767, so it is bit-observable at boundary-crossing inputs despite a sub-millidB spectral footprint.

A saturation/near-saturation detector can therefore serve as a rare, attacker-forceable TRIGGER edge that never fires on normal input, keeping untriggered output bit-identical to the golden filter.

ACCUMULATOR HEADROOM FOR TRIGGER MATH: the filter needs only 32 signed bits but a 40-bit signed accumulator is assumed; 8 spare bits = room for ~510 extra full-scale Q15xQ15 MAC terms. A parallel trigger correlator (e.g. matched-filter detection of a secret watermark/tone sequence) can run in the same/shared datapath without overflow and without perturbing the golden MAC result -- cheap, stealthy added logic.

DETERMINISTIC ROUNDING ASYMMETRY AS FINGERPRINT/SIDE-CHANNEL: round-half-toward-+inf gives a predictable +1 LSB bias versus round-half-even on all exact negative half-way accumulators (acc mod 65536 == 16384).
